name: Liters to Quarts
title: Liters to Quarts: Volume Converter
tutorial: One liter is 1.05669 quarts. The quart and the liter are close neighbours: a US quart is 946 ml, so a liter is about 6 percent more than a quart. A 2-liter bottle of soda is 2.11 quarts, which is just over 8 cups.

The conversion runs one way in practice. Recipes written in liters come from metric kitchens, and the cook reading them has quart cartons and quart pots. A recipe that calls for 3 liters of stock is asking for 3.17 quarts, which is just over three quart cartons.

For rough work, a liter and a quart are interchangeable. The difference is 6 percent, which is smaller than the error in eyeballing a stockpot. For a soup, a stew, or a brine, one quart per liter is close enough. For baking, where liquid ratios matter, use the converter and the exact number.

The quart ladder helps with the rest. A quart is 4 cups, so a liter is 4.23 cups. A quart is 2 pints, so a liter is 2.11 pints. A quart is a quarter of a gallon, so a liter is 0.26 gallons. One conversion opens the whole ladder.

Pot sizes are where the two systems meet. A 6-quart stockpot holds 5.68 liters. A 12-quart stockpot holds 11.36 liters. A recipe that says to use a 5-liter pot is asking for a 5.28-quart pot, which is a 6-quart pot with room to spare.
